problem: Zero-shot VLM navigation agents either carry full visual histories, which fill the context with redundant or distracting observations, or use compact summaries that drop details needed to reconsider earlier decisions. Prior recovery and memory methods do not let retrieved evidence revise the subgoal agenda itself.
motivation: Long-horizon navigation requires revising intermediate objectives, for example when a turn is wrongly marked complete before the intended landmark or a room is misidentified in ObjectNav. Fixing such errors needs a revisable task state and access to evidence that is no longer visible. Selective retrieval sits between full history and compact summaries.
key_idea: Couple a dynamic subgoal agenda with a compact entity-knowledge index over graph-structured visual and geometric episodic memory, so a VLM executive actively retrieves evidence to generate, revise, or reopen subgoals before a skill policy picks the action.
insight: Query-directed retrieval works better than dumping history. The Full Graph variant reaches 62.0 SR against 71.7 for full NavProbe. Retrieval helps (57.3 to 65.0 SR with EKM off in both variants), and consolidating retrieved conclusions into entity summaries adds a further gain (65.0 to 71.7). Retrieval analysis shows queries mostly check action execution (68.4%) and route relations (55.7%), so memory is used to verify instruction progress rather than just to recognize destinations.
method: Task-state memory: an agenda of subgoals, each with a status and verification predicates (confirmed/unconfirmed), plus an execution history. Subgoals can be added, refined, reprioritized, removed, or reopened when contradicted. VLN agendas start from instruction clauses; ObjectNav agendas are built online.
Graph-structured episodic records: a topological graph of place nodes (panoramas), transition edges (trajectories) and landmark entities (detections and locations), plus an occupancy map.
Compressed entity-knowledge index: each entity has a compact textual summary and pointers to its retrievable evidence fields, giving the executive routine context without images.

Task executive (formulate-probe-verify-act): a GPT-5.5 agent reads the observation, task state, and index, then issues entity-field retrieval queries for up to R_max=6 rounds per step. It writes textual conclusions and updates the agenda without moving the robot.
Memory consolidation (EKM): an Entity Knowledge Manager merges query-reference-conclusion records into entity summaries by adding, revising, or deleting claims, without re-opening images.

Skill policy: maps the observation and executive output to GoToWaypoint, VerticalMove, Backtrack, or Stop. Waypoints come from HSGM-style visual waypoints extended with Frontier-Skeleton Sampling on the occupancy map.
Geometric execution: Habitat ShortestPathFollower in simulation; Nav2 on the real robot.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.5 (frozen, role-specific prompts) + YOLO-World landmark detector
setting.observation: RGB-D 960x540, 135° HFOV, four-view panorama at each decision, plus occupancy map/BEV; pose from the simulator
setting.action_space: parameterized skills (GoToWaypoint, VerticalMove, Backtrack, Stop) executed as low-level 0.25 m forward steps via ShortestPathFollower; 40 decisions and 500 actions per episode
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D for VLN-CE, HM3D-v2 for ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: none stated (simulator pose and depth used; ShortestPathFollower executes chosen waypoints)

numbers_note: The HM3D-v2 ObjectNav split and eval-set size are not stated, so 'val' and 'full' are assumptions. Ablation numbers on R2R-CE are in the text and Table 3 but are not listed as separate entries.
results: On a 100-episode R2R-CE subset, NavProbe reaches 71.7 SR and 55.8 SPL, versus 61.7 SR and 45.0 SPL for a GPT-5.5 rerun of Uni-LaViRA. On RxR-CE it reaches 55.3 SR and 38.6 SPL, versus 51.3 and 34.0 for Uni-LaViRA. On HM3D-v2 ObjectNav its SR is 79.3 (vs 77.7 for Uni-LaViRA) but its SPL is lower (43.8 vs 46.1).
limitations: Evaluation is on 100-episode subsets, not full splits, and the main-table baselines mostly use their originally reported numbers, so comparisons are not fully controlled.
Relies on the closed GPT-5.5 model, with multiple retrieval rounds per step (about 1.82 on average when retrieval is used) adding cost; latency and cost are not reported.
Real-robot results are qualitative only, ObjectNav SPL trails Uni-LaViRA, and nDTW on RxR-CE barely improves.
